findings.text: the guard's field list chains to _OP_VOCAB, whose insert_section entry is held against the implementation nowhere — tests/test_mcp_vocabulary_is_complete.py:18 holds op names against _OP_DISPATCH and :26 checks only that id/title/body appear — so a field added to SectionRecord at reckon/_schema.py:852 would leave the vocabulary, the skill prose and the pin green together while only the example, validated against the implementation at tests/test_skill_contracts.py:1453, carried the new field; the claim at :1321-1323 that reading the vocabulary pins the skills to the code is true of op names, not of field lists.

the fragment quotes the declared mutation failing at "assert op in edit — reckon-edit does not name the collapse_section op", which is the pre-repair revision's message; the log it cites, logs/negative-control.log, carries "AssertionError: reckon-edit op reference does not list collapse_section with its required fields" at tests/test_skill_contracts.py:1354, so the evidence record reproduces a message that appears in no artefact it cites.

FIXED_READ_SET_TOKEN_BUDGET rises 15_350 to 15_500 to carry the 112-token worked-examples block, against the same test's message at :687 that worked examples are reference material which moves to references/; moving the block leaves 15,298 estimated tokens under the 15_350 bound, so the raise spends attention the file's own rule says is recoverable — named rather than scored as a defect because the reason is recorded and the examples are what a coordinator copies at the landing beat.

the manifest names its two gate arms under tests and test_logs rather than the armed-only baseline_suite/after_suite fields, so reckon/crew/review.py:1201 read_review annotates every stored record for this run with added_failure_count null and an unmeasured note while the stored record carries the derived 0 — two answers to one question, and the review fence at prompt.txt:59 asks for the count under exactly those two field names.
